solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Barnaby's sin, I abhor, showing up the old country

indicators.note: something showing up in these words appears among their letters, run across the word breaks

explanation.surface: Someone loathes a character's sin, and that loathing exposes the old country they came from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'showing up' signals that the answer sits in plain sight across 'Barnaby's sin, I abhor', ignoring the apostrophe and comma.
explanation.definitionFit: Abyssinia is the former name of Ethiopia, so it is an old country in a historical sense.

clue.text: Light, graceful Cockney's needing a shave?

indicators.note: a Cockney speaker traditionally drops the initial aitch, so the word loses its first letter

parts.note: someone needing a shave is hairy

explanation.surface: A light, graceful Londoner whose stubble has grown out.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys, the working-class Londoners of the East End, are known for not sounding an initial H.
explanation.definitionFit: Something light and graceful in movement or style is described as airy, a common synonym.

clue.text: Year with no euro for change? I accept the challenge!

indicators.note: the letters of the words are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: A traveller agrees to go a year without using euros as currency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for change' looks like a reference to coins, but it signals rearranging NO EURO into OUREON.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying you're on is an informal idiom for agreeing to a dare or wager.

clue.text: Son and father meeting in the spring

parts.note: pa is an informal word for one's father

explanation.surface: A son and his father arrange to meet each other in springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the spring' looks like the season, but it is a mineral water source.
explanation.definitionFit: A spa is a place built around a mineral spring, or the spring itself.

clue.text: Extra dance cancelled?

parts.note: something cancelled is called off, so there is 'no' event
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: Is an additional dance now called off?
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a no-ball is an illegal delivery by the bowler, which gives the batting side an extra run.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket extra is a run not scored off the bat, and an illegal delivery is one kind.

clue.text: Part of Mediterranean an eagle has nested at regularly

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals means every other letter, starting with the first

explanation.surface: An eagle has built its nest somewhere on the Mediterranean coast.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea between Greece and Turkey is an arm of the Mediterranean.

clue.text: I'd to desert very bright boy or girl

indicators.note: letters that desert a word leave it, so they are removed

parts.note: a vivid colour is very bright

explanation.surface: Someone had to abandon a dazzling child.
explanation.definitionFit: Viv is a short form of both Vivian and Vivienne, so it can be a name for either sex.

clue.text: Idea mostly incorporated into very old film

indicators.note: something incorporated into another thing is taken inside it
most of the word, so its final letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A notion has largely been worked into an ancient movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims Idea to IDE, which goes between V and O.
explanation.definitionFit: A video is a recorded film, as a noun, or the act of recording one.

clue.text: Not allowed to check Oxford English Dictionary

parts.note: to vet something is to check it carefully

explanation.surface: Someone is forbidden from looking words up in the great dictionary.
explanation.definitionFit: A proposal that is vetoed has been rejected or forbidden by someone with authority.

clue.text: Regret insult being overheard? Nonsense!

indicators.note: words that are overheard are caught by the ear, so the spoken form counts

parts.note: to rue something is to regret it; a barb is a cutting remark or insult

explanation.surface: Someone is sorry that their rude comment was heard by others.
explanation.walkthrough: RUE BARB spoken sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhubarb is British slang for nonsense, from the word actors mutter to sound like background chatter.

clue.text: Turned to hound one awaited in play

indicators.note: turned round, the combined words are read backwards

parts.note: a hound is a dog

explanation.surface: Someone switched to a hunting dog while waiting for a character in a play.
explanation.definitionFit: In Beckett's play Waiting for Godot, the title character is awaited but never comes.

clue.text: "Don't make it any worse" we all tell one messing about

indicators.note: letters messed about are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: We all warn someone who is fooling around not to make matters worse.
explanation.definitionFit: To let well alone is an idiom meaning to avoid interfering in case things get worse.

clue.text: Criminal dog owner twisted terrier's tail

indicators.note: twisted words have their letters bent into a new order
the tail of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A dodgy dog owner wrings his terrier's tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twisted' rearranges DOG OWNER into WRONGDOE; R is the end of terrier.
explanation.definitionFit: A criminal is someone who breaks the law, which a wrongdoer does by definition.

clue.text: Ruin the party for nations of the world?

parts.note: the UN, the United Nations, gathers the world's countries
a do is an informal word for a party

explanation.surface: Someone wrecks a celebration organised for the world's nations.
explanation.definitionFit: To undo someone or something is to ruin it, as in 'his pride was his undoing'.

clue.text: Distress call — nothing that could render you indifferent

parts.note: SOS is the international distress signal
O, the figure zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: Getting no answer to an emergency call might leave you cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Something so-so is mediocre, neither good nor bad, which is one sense of indifferent.

clue.text: Singers transformed a prison

indicators.note: transformed letters are changed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A jail has been changed so that it now holds vocalists.
explanation.definitionFit: Soprani is the Italian plural of soprano, the highest singing voices.

clue.text: Material simply, at the end, the opposite of 1 down

parts.note: stuff is cloth or material

indicators.note: the end of the word gives just its final letter

explanation.surface: Plain cloth turns out in the end to be the reverse of an earlier answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 1 down is AIRY; a stuffy room lacks fresh air.
explanation.definitionFit: A stuffy place is close and badly ventilated, the opposite of a light and breezy one.

clue.text: Making mistake, cutting head off fish

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, which is cut away

parts.note: a herring is a fish

explanation.surface: Someone is going wrong while beheading a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Erring is the present participle of err, to make a mistake.

clue.text: Very keen to shoot horse in film, and dwarf

parts.note: Trigger was the horse of cowboy star Roy Rogers in his films
Happy is one of the seven dwarfs in Snow White

explanation.surface: A screen horse and a little helper are both eager to start shooting the film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shoot' reads as filming in the surface, but the answer means firing a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone trigger-happy is too ready to fire a gun, or by extension to act rashly.

clue.text: Very little land surrounded by water gets leased out

definitions.text: Very little land surrounded by water

parts.note: 'gets leased out' means 'is let', so gets stands for is
a property leased out is let

explanation.surface: A tiny bit of land in the sea is rented out.
explanation.definitionFit: An islet is a very small island, which is land with water all round it.

clue.text: Short platform for men only

indicators.note: a word cut short loses its last letter

parts.note: a stage is a raised platform

explanation.surface: A low platform reserved for male users.
explanation.definitionFit: A stag party or stag night is a celebration attended by men alone.

clue.text: Sheet of paper from loo, if recycled

indicators.note: recycled material is reprocessed into a new form, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A sheet of paper might come from toilet tissue if it were recycled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loo' is British slang for a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: A folio is a sheet of paper folded once, or a single leaf of a book.

clue.text: Popular former routine is wide of the mark

parts.note: something in is fashionable or popular
ex is a prefix meaning former
an act is a performer's routine

explanation.surface: A once-popular stage routine now misses its target.
explanation.definitionFit: Something wide of the mark is not accurate, which is what inexact means.

clue.text: Film about fine little amphibian

indicators.note: one piece goes about the other, surrounding it

parts.note: E.T. is the Spielberg film about an alien
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: A film about a lovely small frog or newt.
explanation.definitionFit: An eft is a young newt, a small amphibian.

clue.text: Legendary creature, lacking tail however

indicators.note: a word lacking its tail has its last letter removed

parts.note: the yeti is the legendary abominable snowman of the Himalayas

explanation.surface: A mythical beast, though without its tail.
explanation.definitionFit: Yet and however are synonyms as conjunctions introducing a contrast.

clue.text: Moral victory by good Conservative

parts.note: something moral is right
a win is a victory

explanation.surface: A virtuous triumph by a decent Tory candidate.
explanation.definitionFit: Conservative politics belongs to the political right, so its wing of a party is the right.
